To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

Hsp90 stabilizes the native state of citrate synthase under heat shock conditions and that this function is based on the transient binding of Hsp90 to highly structured early folding intermediates of citrate synthases.

the Hsp90 chaperone family stabilizes the native structure of a substrate protein by transiently binding and releasing early folding intermediates, which otherwise would undergo irreversible aggregation.

Hsp90 transiently interacts with highly structured early unfolding intermediate states of citrate synthase, which are formed under conditions of elevated temperature, and that these interactions stabilize the active enzyme species by preventing irreversible aggregation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the function and mechanism of the heat shock protein (Hsp) 90, a major chaperone of the cytosol.
the function and the mechanism of action of Hsp90 in vivo and in particular under heat-shock conditions.
the elucidation of the function of Hsc/Hsp90 under heat-shock conditions in vitro and in vivo, and with the molecular basis for this function.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Hsp90 protein is an ATP-dependent protein chaperone which binds to highly structured early intermediates of protein unfolding.
Hsp90 stabilizes proteins by transient binding to their early unfolding intermediates and thus prevents their irreversible aggregation.
Hsp90 acts as a molecular chaperone in vivo, and in vitro.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have demonstrated that Hsp90 is not a chaperone in the strict sense of the word, but rather a “stabilizing factor”.
the Hsp90 chaperones are not involved in the folding of the substrate protein but in the protection against the aggregation of the substrate protein.
Hsp90 acts like a molecular chaperone, but it is different from the other molecular chaperones, because it does not bind to denatured polypeptides but to highly structured early intermediates.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Hsp90 chaperone is able to bind and stabilize early unfolding intermediates of citrate synthase.
Hsp90 is a very versatile chaperone.
the Hsp90 chaperone system is not just a passive stabilizer of proteins, but that it actively prevents aggregation of proteins by transient interactions with partially folded species.
